title: Pullback preserves finite Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, $n\geq1$, and
put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $K\in D^b_c(Y,A)$ be a
bounded constructible
complex of finite Tor amplitude
in $[a,b]$. Then $Lf^*K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ is bounded constructible and has
finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. Consequently $Lf^*$ carries
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ into $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, which is clause (i) of
the finite-Tor preservation summary at the finite coefficient stages.

proof.text: Specialize the finite coefficient datum to $\mathcal O_E$ and $I=(\varpi_E)$, so $P_j=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^j$ and $P_n=A$. The coefficient data [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field and finite quotients; a principal ideal domain is Noetherian because every ideal is principal. The residue quotient is finite, hence additive torsion, and [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] supplies perfectness of every $P_j$ by the two-term finite free resolution. The extension of the $\ell$-adic valuation gives $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $e\geq1$ and $u$ a unit, so every $P_j$ is killed by $\ell^j$; these orders are invertible on $X,Y$ because $\ell\ne p$. Thus the coefficient hypotheses in [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible] hold. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], clause (ii), the intrinsic bounded constructible category in the item agrees with the category defined by etale origin used in that lemma, on both $Y$ and $X$. Apply the lemma with $g=f$ to obtain $Lf^*K\in D^b_c(X,A)$. It remains to prove the Tor bound.

Apply [lem-sf-flat-model] to the assumed Tor amplitude of $K$. We obtain an isomorphism $K\cong P$ in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, where $P$ is a bounded complex of flat $A_Y$-module sheaves and $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$.

The model $P$ of Step 2 is bounded above by $b$ and termwise flat. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] on $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_Y)$ to make its K-flatness explicit. Regard $f$ as the morphism of ringed pro-etale sites with constant-coefficient isomorphism $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ from [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] now applies: $Q=f^*P=f^{-1}P\otimes_{f^{-1}A_Y}A_X$ is K-flat and has flat terms. The constant-coefficient isomorphism identifies $Q$ termwise with $f^{-1}P$, and $Q^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$ because inverse image sends zero to zero. The same derived-pullback definition says that exact $f^{-1}$ computes $Lf^*$ on any representative. Applying this derived functor to the isomorphism $K\cong P$ therefore gives $Lf^*K\cong Q$; no chain map $P\to K$ is assumed.

source.place: ## Proof, derived pullback and flatness paragraph

proof.text: For an arbitrary sheaf $N$ of $A_X$-modules in degree zero, the K-flat computation [def-weil-derived-tensor] and Step 3 give $Lf^*K\otimes_A^LN\cong Q\otimes_AN$. Its degree-$q$ term is $Q^q\otimes_AN$, which is zero outside $[a,b]$. For any such $q$, both the kernel of the outgoing differential and the image of the incoming differential are subobjects of the zero term, so $\mathcal H^q(Q\otimes_AN)=0$. This holds for every $N$, hence is precisely Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Combining with Step 1 gives the assertion. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ choose an interval from that definition and apply the assertion to put $Lf^*K$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$.
